summary_en: Introduces an accelerated physics-informed neural-network framework for ultrafast ultrasound blood-flow imaging. SeqPINN discretizes time in the Navier-Stokes formulation and solves sequentially with test-time adaptation, while SP-PINN supports parallel training and uncertainty-aware inference. Finite-element and vessel-phantom experiments report blood-flow RMSEs of 0.63/0.81 cm/s in a straight vessel and 1.07/1.41 cm/s in a trifurcate vessel for SeqPINN/SP-PINN, respectively, while substantially accelerating training over vanilla PINNs.

summary_en: Develops a deep-learning ultrasonic computed-tomography pipeline for nondestructive testing of workpieces. A linear-array USCT platform supplies cross-sectional ultrasonic measurements, and an attention-enhanced HAU2Net with a hybrid-scale loss learns fast sound-speed/image inversion from 9,985 simulated and 405 real sound-speed/wavefield pairs. The reported reconstruction runs at near-real-time speed and is evaluated against K-Wave and several neural reconstruction baselines under simulated, noisy, and real measurements.

summary_en: Formulates ultrafast Doppler ultrasound blood-flow estimation and tissue-motion compensation as a joint convex inverse problem. Blood-flow, tissue, and motion components are estimated together with component-specific regularization using an alternating proximal forward-backward algorithm; a multiresolution strategy handles larger tissue motions. Synthetic and in-vivo experiments show cleaner flow estimation in the presence of moving tissue than separate or uncompensated processing.
